clue.text: Article with two pages to conclude one Times supplement

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
P is the abbreviation for page, so two of them make PP
to conclude is to end something
I is the Roman numeral for one
the multiplication sign, read as 'times', is X

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor fills the last page of a Times supplement with one more article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is the multiplication sign X.
explanation.definitionFit: An appendix is extra matter added at the back of a book, a kind of supplement.

clue.text: Helpless cheers following a defeat

indicators.note: following means the word for cheers comes after the a

parts.note: TA is informal British for thanks, like cheers
a loss is a defeat

explanation.surface: Supporters cheer feebly after their team is beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone bewildered and unable to act, helpless.

clue.text: Student held back by slip-ups

indicators.note: back means the held letters are read from right to left
held says the letters are contained inside the words given

explanation.surface: A learner is set back by mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held' finds LIPUP inside 'slip-ups', and 'back' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil is a learner at school, a student.

clue.text: Hazardous substance that could make us clean water

indicators.note: could make means the letters could be rearranged into another phrase

explanation.surface: An ironic warning that a toxin might turn into clean water for us.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear waste is radioactive material left over from reactors, highly dangerous.

clue.text: Enter island by rickety punt

indicators.note: rickety means shaky, so the letters of punt are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone lands on an island in an unsteady flat-bottomed boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To input data is to enter it into a computer.

clue.text: Caterpillar food

definitions.meaning: a larva of an insect, such as a maggot or caterpillar
informal word for something to eat

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an insect larva and, colloquially, something to eat.

clue.text: Winding in loop, catching slippery fish

indicators.note: catching means the loop surrounds the fish

parts.note: a ring is a loop
an eel is a notoriously slippery fish

explanation.surface: An angler winds in a line with a loop, hooking an eel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winding' looks like reeling in a line, but means staggered or dazed.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeling describes being stunned or staggering, as if from a blow that winds you.

clue.text: Noble — like The Wasteland being recited

indicators.note: being recited means the word is spoken, giving a similar-sounding one

parts.note: a waste land is barren, as in T. S. Eliot's poem

explanation.surface: An aristocrat reads Eliot's poem aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron is a member of the lowest rank of the peerage, a nobleman.

clue.text: Hit back with clubs, breaking up truncheon

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

indicators.note: breaking means the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A brawl where someone retaliates with clubs, smashing a police baton.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterpunch is a retaliatory blow, a hit given in return.

clue.text: A photo capturing starter of strawberry jelly

indicators.note: capturing means 'A photo' together holds the next piece between its two parts

parts.note: PIC is short for picture, a photo

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A snapshot of a strawberry jelly, perhaps for a food blog.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly made from meat stock, used to set cold dishes.

clue.text: One breaking into jetty is adventurous type

indicators.note: breaking into means the word One is placed inside the word for jetty

parts.note: a pier is a jetty projecting into the sea

explanation.surface: Someone forcing their way onto a jetty is described as a daring sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer is an explorer or early settler, someone bold who goes first.

clue.text: That hurts large hooter

parts.note: OW is the cry of someone in pain
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a big loud horn is painful to hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooter' suggests a car horn or a nose, but here it is a bird that hoots.
explanation.definitionFit: Owls are known for their hooting call, so a hooter is a playful name for the bird.

clue.text: No. sixteen fouled in extra time

indicators.note: fouled suggests something messed up, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A football commentary: the number sixteen player commits a foul during extra time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fouled' rearranges the letters of NO SIXTEEN; 'No.' supplies N and O.
explanation.definitionFit: An extension is additional time granted, as when a deadline or match is prolonged.

clue.text: Throw around stray alcoholic drink

indicators.note: around means the word for throw goes round the word for stray

parts.note: to shy is to throw, as at a coconut shy
to err is to stray from the right path

explanation.surface: Someone tosses about a wandering glass of booze.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherry is a fortified wine from southern Spain, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Charm displayed by liking going topless

indicators.note: going topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a penchant is a liking or fondness

explanation.surface: Allure shown by a fondness for going without a top.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant is to delight or bewitch, to charm.

clue.text: Pub holds onto protein-rich food for down-and-out

indicators.note: holds onto means the word for pub contains the food

parts.note: a bar is a pub
an egg is a food rich in protein

explanation.surface: A pub keeps hold of its nourishing snacks for a homeless person.
explanation.definitionFit: A beggar is a destitute person asking for alms, a vagrant or derelict.

clue.text: Once again tend to fall back

definitions.meaning: to treat a patient a second time

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two parts it means treat again; as one word it means withdraw.

clue.text: Ecstatic sound of famous singer, Joe, and band

indicators.note: sound of says the singer's surname is said aloud, giving its spoken form

parts.note: Joe Cocker was a famous English rock singer
a hoop is a circular band

explanation.surface: Delight at hearing Joe Cocker sing with his group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' looks like Cocker's backing group, but it is a ring of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cock-a-hoop is an idiom for jubilant and boastfully delighted.

clue.text: Uncle Arthur not entirely lucid

indicators.note: not entirely says only part of the words is taken

explanation.surface: An elderly relative is somewhat confused.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucid and clear both mean easy to understand.

clue.text: Our welcoming cricket club brings spring to mind

indicators.note: welcoming means our takes the club inside it

explanation.surface: Our hospitality to a cricket club makes us think of springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: When an idea occurs to you, it comes to mind unbidden.

clue.text: Mineral stream

definitions.meaning: a hard black lignite used in jewellery
a fast narrow flow of liquid or gas from a nozzle

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a black gemstone mineral and a forceful spurt of fluid.

clue.text: John's opening a company with B Epstein, perhaps

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: John Lennon starting a company with Beatles manager Brian Epstein.
explanation.walkthrough: 'B Epstein' suggests Brian Epstein, the Beatles' manager; the definition is the sculptor Jacob Epstein.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Jacob Epstein was a sculptor, so Epstein is an example of someone bearing this first name.

clue.text: New form of lace — it's stretchy

indicators.note: a new form of the letters means they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dressmaker praises a novel kind of lace for its give.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastic describes material that stretches and springs back.

clue.text: Opening portion of macaroni cheese

indicators.note: portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Starting with a helping of macaroni cheese, as at a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' reads as the start of a meal but is the definition, a recess.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a recess or gap in a wall, an opening for a statue.

clue.text: Sacred act — it's covered in religious education

indicators.note: covered in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: RE is the school subject Religious Education
it, with the 's (is) acting as a link

explanation.surface: A sacred ceremony is taught in a school's religion lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is Religious Education, a British school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite is a ceremonial religious act such as baptism.

clue.text: Stop for welcome morsel

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
hi is a greeting, a welcome
a bit is a small piece, a morsel

explanation.surface: Someone stops in for a bite to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: To prohibit is to forbid or ban, i.e. to stop something happening.
